newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses storm to new closing records.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses storm to new closing records.

text.p: British and German shares ended at record highs on Friday, celebrating exceptionally positive U.S. inflation data and a rampant Wall Street.

New data showed U.S. retail sales rising a modest 0.2 percent and consumer prices rising only 0.1 percent in August despite real earnings up 0.7 percent, severely undermining expectations of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates.

European bourses hailed the news, Frankfurt and London pushing their indices to new highs, and holding their gains as Wall Street joined the party in the European midafternoon smashing its May 22 record.

"It appears we have the best of both possible worlds -- good modest economic growth and the absence of inflationary pressures," said Value Line Asset Management chief investment officer Philip Orlando.

The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of Britain's 100 largest companies set a new high of 3,970.5 points in afternoon dealings, up 37.9 points on the day and bringing its gain for the week to 77.5 points.

At the European close the Dow Industrial average was up 52 points, while London closed up 35 points, Frankfurt was up 26 points, and the IBIS DAX had broken the lofty 2,600 level. Now London's next target will be to push the FTSE over the 4,000 level and keep it there.
A rise in interest rates had been widely expected from a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's September 24 Federal Open Market Committee.

"A fortnight ago everyone was worried that interest rates would go up in excess of a quarter point, now there's a chance that there will be no rise this time around and the FTSE is looking to go to 4,000 points," a dealer said.

Although far from breaking records, Paris's CAC-40 also relished the U.S. news, reversing morning slippage and closing a solid 15 points ahead, breaking through a technical resistance point on the way. The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,085 from 2,070.5 on Thursday's close. Volume was a busy 5.67 billion francs.
U.S., German and British government bonds all rallied on the U.S. inflation news, adding vigour to the stock markets' response.
But the much-reduced likelihood of a rise in U.S. interest rates pushed the dollar to session lows, although solid buying on the dips helped to maintain its poise.
Some players had forecast a 50 basis point (0.5 percentage point) rise in U.S. interest rates from the FOMC meeting, but this is now questionable given the data and imminent presidential election.

"The data has eased some of the aggressive rate hike speculation for a 50 basis point hike, but the feeling is that a 25 basis points rise might still be on the cards," said Brian Kiely at Royal Bank of Scotland.
In the oil market Iraq tension held up prices. World benchmark Brent crude oil futures traded as high as $24.11 a barrel, up 24 cents on the day. It achieved a high of $24.27 earlier in the day.
"I wouldn't be a seller in this market. If there is action over the weekend then prices will rally again," said Peter Bogin at Cambridge Energy Research Associates in Paris.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5122 marks and 110.40 yen compared with late Thursday's 1.5129 and 110.11.
STOCK MARKET CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares closed up 35.3 at 3,967.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 15 points at 2,080.37.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index closed 25.64 points up at 2,595.96. The IBIS DAX electronic trading index closed up 26.46 at 2,614.50.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $383.10 vs $382.30 on Thursday, uneasy ahead of IMF meeting on possible gold sales. Silver ended firmer at $5.07, up five cents with gold.
